title: observability: token-level KV enhanced logging, metrics, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Add token-level KV logging + metrics, new token cost/latency/KV dashboards, tuned alerts and runbook. Backwards-compatible telemetry changes; no API break.
description:
Context and motivation: We need better visibility into per-token cost and latency interactions with KV cache behavior for high-throughput workloads. Current dashboards only show aggregated per-request metrics which obscure cases where KV cache hit/miss patterns correlate with token cost regressions. This PR introduces token-level KV logging, exposes new per-route token cost/latency/KV metrics, adds Grafana dashboards, and tunes alerts and runbook guidance for SREs and on-call engineers.

What this changes: 1) Add structured token-level KV logging (lightweight, sampled by route and sequence-length buckets) in services/serving/runtime to capture kv_hit, kv_evict, token_index, cumulative_token_cost, and token_latency_ms. 2) Emit derived metrics (token_count, token_cost_usd, token_latency_ms_p50/p95, kv_cache_hit_rate) with tags for route/model/quantization_profile. 3) New Grafana dashboards (token_kv_overview, token_cost_latency_breakdown, kv_hit_breakdown) with panel links to traces and runbook anchors. 4) Alert tuning: adjust thresholds for token_cost and kv_hit_rate, add a composite alert that suppresses noisy signals during known scale events, and provide a short runbook for escalation and mitigation.

Backward compatibility and safety: Logging is opt-in sampling (default 0.1%) and controlled by feature flags and per-customer sampling config; metrics are additive and do not change existing metric names. No changes to public API surfaces.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for logging schema and metrics aggregation added; integration test simulates variable KV hit patterns and verifies metric labels and dashboard panels render expected values; load test on canary cluster showed ~0.6% CPU overhead at 0.1% sampling. CI flakiness on e2e (initial) addressed by mocking tracing backend.

Rollout plan: Feature-flagged rollout to staged -> canary (10%) -> all clusters over 48 hours. Dashboard will be added to the monitoring stack and annotated with runbook links. Alerts will be enabled in staged first with 24h evaluation window before prod enablement.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the logging schema (services/serving/runtime/logging/kv_schema.md), metric cardinality controls, and alert suppression logic (monitoring/alerts/token_kv_alerts.yaml).
